subject: apple snail
title: A Snail Lost an Eye Built Like Yours. A Month Later It Was Back

scenes.text: A snail lost its eye. A month later, it was back.
Not a simple eye spot. It has a cornea, a lens and a retina, like yours.
The wound heals in a day. By day fifteen, every part is back, even the optic nerve.
How? In 2025, scientists found this snail shares a master eye gene with us, pax6.
Switch off both copies in an embryo, and the snail grows no eyes at all.
Same eye, same gene. The snail regrows it. Scientists now want to know why you can't.

description:
A 2025 Nature Communications study from UC Davis showed the golden apple snail, Pomacea canaliculata, fully regrows an amputated camera-type eye, with cornea, lens and retina, in about a month.
The team also used CRISPR to show the pax6 gene, which controls eye development in humans too, is essential for the snail's eyes.
Which animal regrowth surprises you most?
first_comment: Back in 1766 a researcher noticed beheaded garden snails could regrow their whole heads. Would you want this power?
